function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a practical roadmap you can follow to build an LLM that answers questions about Islam. I’ll cover everything from data gathering to fine‑tuning, evaluation, safety, and deployment. Feel free to skip sections that already fit your workflow. --- ## 1️⃣ Define Scope & Constraints | Item | Why it matters | Practical tip | |------|----------------|---------------| | **Target audience** | Determines tone, depth, and language (e.g., scholars vs. laypeople). | Ask yourself: “Will this be a study aid, a public FAQ, or a personal tutor?” | | **Allowed content** | Must comply with OpenAI policy (no extremist propaganda, no hateful content). | Create a *content policy* checklist:
• No extremist or violent content.
• No personal data or private info.
• No political persuasion. | | **Legal & ethical** | Avoid copyright infringement and respect religious sensitivities. | Use only public domain or properly licensed texts. For copyrighted works, obtain licenses or use excerpts under fair‑use (e.g., short quotes). | --- ## 2️⃣ Build a High‑Quality Dataset ### 2.1 Sources | Source | Type | Notes | |--------|------|-------| | **Quran (public domain)** | Text | Use the *Sahih International* translation or other public‑domain versions. | | **Hadith collections** | Text | e.g., *Sahih Bukhari*, *Sahih Muslim* (public domain). | | **Scholarly Q&A** | QA pairs | Look for open‑source Q&A datasets (e.g., “IslamicQA” on HuggingFace). | | **Academic papers** | Summaries | Use arXiv or open‑access journals on Islamic studies. | | **Community forums** | Conversational data | Scrape public Q&A sites (e.g., islamqa.info) – but filter for quality and remove spam. | | **Glossaries & Encyclopedias** | Definitions | e.g., *Encyclopaedia of Islam* (public domain). | ### 2.2 Preprocessing Pipeline ```python import re from datasets import load_dataset, DatasetDict def clean_text(text): # Remove footnotes, bracketed citations, and excessive whitespace text = re.sub(r'\[\d+\]', '', text) # [1], [23] text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text).strip() return text def preprocess(example): example['clean'] = clean_text(example['text']) return example raw_ds = load_dataset('my_custom_raw') # Your raw scraped data clean_ds = raw_ds.map(preprocess, batched=False) ``` ### 2.3 Format for Fine‑Tuning For instruction‑tuned models, use the *prefix–suffix* format: ```json { "instruction": "Explain the concept of Tawheed.", "input": "", "output": "Tawheed is the Islamic doctrine of monotheism..." } ``` If you have question–answer pairs, convert them similarly: ```json { "instruction": "Answer the following question:", "input": "What is the significance of Ramadan?", "output": "Ramadan is the month of fasting..." } ``` Store the cleaned dataset as a `DatasetDict` with splits (`train`, `validation`, `test`). --- ## 3️⃣ Choose a Base Model | Option | Pros | Cons | Typical size | |--------|------|------|--------------| | **Open‑source LLM (e.g., LLaMA‑2, GPT‑NeoX, Falcon)** | Free, modifiable, no API limits | Requires GPU/TPU resources | 7B–13B (good trade‑off) | | **Commercial API (OpenAI GPT‑4, Anthropic Claude)** | Managed infrastructure, high performance | Cost per token, limited customizability | 8k–32k context window | **Recommendation:** Start with **LLaMA‑2‑7B** (or 13B if you have the compute). It’s open‑source, has a permissive license, and performs well on instruction tasks after fine‑tuning. --- ## 4️⃣ Fine‑Tune the Model ### 4.1 Environment Setup ```bash conda create -n islml python=3.11 conda activate islml pip install transformers datasets accelerate bitsandbytes trl ``` ### 4.2 LoRA (Low‑Rank Adaptation) LoRA allows you to fine‑tune a small number of parameters while keeping the base weights frozen—great for limited GPU memory. ```python from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, Trainer, TrainingArguments from trl import LoRAConfig, get_peft_model model_name = "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_name, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto", trust_remote_code=True ) lora_config = LoRAConfig( r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], # adjust based on architecture lora_dropout=0.05, bias="none", task_type="CAUSAL_LM" ) model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config) ``` ### 4.3 Tokenization & Dataset Preparation ```python max_length = 512 def tokenize(example): prompt = f"{example['instruction']} {example['input']}" inputs = tokenizer(prompt, truncation=True, max_length=max_length, padding='max_length') outputs = tokenizer(example['output'], truncation=True, max_length=max_length, padding='max_length') inputs["labels"] = outputs["input_ids"] return inputs tokenized_ds = clean_ds.map(tokenize, batched=True, remove_columns=clean_ds.column_names) ``` ### 4.4 Training Arguments ```python training_args = TrainingArguments( output_dir="./islm_output", num_train_epochs=3, per_device_train_batch_size=4, gradient_accumulation_steps=8, learning_rate=5e-5, fp16=True, logging_steps=50, save_strategy="epoch", evaluation_strategy="epoch", eval_steps=None, report_to="tensorboard", push_to_hub=False ) trainer = Trainer( model=model, args=training_args, train_dataset=tokenized_ds["train"], eval_dataset=tokenized_ds["validation"], tokenizer=tokenizer ) trainer.train() ``` > **Tip:** If you hit OOM, reduce `per_device_train_batch_size` or increase `gradient_accumulation_steps`. --- ## 5️⃣ Evaluate & Iterate | Metric | How to compute | What to look for | |--------|----------------|------------------| | **Perplexity** | `trainer.evaluate()` | Lower perplexity → better language modeling. | | **BLEU / ROUGE** | Compare generated answers to reference answers | Higher scores → closer to human‑written responses. | | **Human Evaluation** | Sample 100 QA pairs, rate relevance, correctness, tone | Identify hallucinations or misinterpretations. | | **Safety Checks** | Run through a moderation pipeline (OpenAI Moderation API or local classifier) | Flag any extremist or hateful content. | If you notice systematic errors (e.g., over‑generalizing or missing nuance), augment the dataset with more examples covering those edge cases. --- ## 6️⃣ Safety & Moderation Layer Even after fine‑tuning, add a post‑generation filter: ```python import openai def moderate(text): resp = openai.Moderation.create(input=text) return resp["results"][0]["flagged"] def safe_generate(prompt): raw = trainer.model.generate(**tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(trainer.args.device)) answer = tokenizer.decode(raw[0], skip_special_tokens=True) if moderate(answer): return "I’m sorry, I can’t help with that." return answer ``` Alternatively, use a lightweight local classifier (e.g., `transformers.AutoModelForSequenceClassification`) trained on labeled extremist/non‑extremist text. --- ## 7️⃣ Deployment Options | Option | Pros | Cons | Example stack | |--------|------|------|---------------| | **Self‑hosted (Docker + FastAPI)** | Full control, no external costs | Requires server maintenance | Docker image, uvicorn, gunicorn | | **Managed inference (vLLM, ExLlama)** | Low latency, auto‑scale | Still needs GPU | vLLM + FastAPI | | **Cloud provider (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI)** | Managed scaling, monitoring | Vendor lock‑in, cost | SageMaker Endpoint | | **API gateway + Lambda** | Serverless, pay‑as‑you‑go | Cold starts, limited runtime | AWS API Gateway + Lambda (Python) | **Sample FastAPI endpoint** ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from pydantic import BaseModel app = FastAPI() class Query(BaseModel): question: str @app.post("/ask") async def ask(q: Query): prompt = f"Answer the following question:\n{q.question}\nAnswer:" answer = safe_generate(prompt) return {"answer": answer} ``` Deploy with Docker: ```dockerfile FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install -r requirements.txt COPY . . CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "80"] ``` --- ## 8️⃣ Continuous Improvement 1. **Collect user feedback** – add a “Was this helpful?” button. 2. **Log queries & responses** – anonymize and store for future retraining. 3. **Periodic re‑fine‑tune** – every 3–6 months with new data or updated scholarship. 4. **Monitor for drift** – track perplexity and safety flag rates over time. --- ## 9️⃣ Resources & References | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | **HuggingFace Datasets** | https://huggingface.co/datasets | | **Open‑source LLMs** | https://huggingface.co/models?search=llama | | **LoRA implementation** | https://github.com/huggingface/peft | | **IslamicQA dataset** | https://huggingface.co/datasets/islamicqa | | **OpenAI Moderation API** | https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/moderation | | **vLLM** | https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm | | **ExLlama** | https://github.com/turboderp/exllama | --- ### Quick Checklist Before Launch - [ ] Dataset is clean, balanced, and respects copyright. - [ ] Model passes internal safety tests (moderation, no extremist content). - [ ] Human evaluation shows >90% correct answers on a random sample. - [ ] Deployment includes rate limiting and logging. - [ ] You have a plan for collecting and incorporating user feedback. Good luck building your Islamic knowledge assistant! If you hit a specific roadblock (e.g., dataset cleaning, LoRA config, deployment), let me know and I can dive deeper into that step.
